traps.no_artist: There is no artist and no title — an object NAME ('Cigar mold') and a material ('Wood'). §4.2's tombstone form and §7's created_by edge both assume an author. A city history museum is full of objects that have none. See D23.
traps.suffix_is_physical: A-B are the mold's two halves, plainly visible in the work photograph. Stripping the suffix to get 48.108.14 identifies a different thing; treating '48.108.14A-B' as opaque loses that it is two pieces. See D24.
traps.period_phrase_date: 'late 19th century' is neither a year nor a year range. EDTF can express it, but only after a vocabulary maps the phrase. Distinct from 'ca. 1774' (D16), which is a year with an approximation marker.
traps.estate_donor: Third donor type after person and organization. 'Gift from the Estate of Mrs. Pauline Stein' names a legal entity standing in for a deceased person — an extractor taking the last personal name produces a living donor who does not exist.
traps.adjacent_panel: Shot from far enough back to include a neighbouring black panel serving different objects. 24 of 64 lines flagged as clipped, nearly all from that second panel. Text from two panels interleaved in one reading.

case_contents_glimpsed.note: One vitrine, many objects, MIXED OWNERSHIP. Some MCNY-owned with accessions, some lent privately with none at all.
